annotations.text:
A REALLY GOOD TRADE SITE

Different premise, not a re-skin. Everything before this was an agency site. This is built for someone 45-70 with a driveway, deciding whether to let a stranger take £8k off them.

What changed, and why:

• NO PRICES, by your call. The service cards carry no figures. What stays is the promise around pricing — free survey, fixed written quote, no day rates — which does much of the same trust work without committing you to a number.
• PHONE NUMBER EVERYWHERE. Top bar, header in 25px orange, hero button, final CTA, footer. On mobile a sticky call bar that never scrolls away. That bar alone typically does more than the rest of the site combined.
• REVIEWS WITH NAMES, TOWNS AND DATES, badged as verified Google reviews. Anonymous testimonials read as invented.
• 17px BODY TEXT, not 15px. High contrast. Your customers wear reading glasses.
• ORDINARY LAYOUT. Header, hero, trust row, services, process, work, reviews, areas, CTA, footer. Familiar on purpose — people know where to look, so nothing gets missed.
• AREAS COVERED as a real list. Doubles as the internal linking the SEO plan needs.
• BUTTONS THAT LOOK LIKE BUTTONS — solid orange, slight drop shadow, obvious affordance.

Colours: deep green #17352a (established, unfussy), burnt orange #c2410c for every action, warm off-white ground.
Type: Bitter for headings (sturdy slab, reads traditional without being fussy), Libre Franklin for body (plainly readable).

This is deliberately unfashionable. It should look like the most credible gate company in the area, not the most designed.

MOBILE

Most of your enquiries will arrive on this. Someone is standing on their driveway holding a phone.

• Sticky bottom bar: Call now / Get a quote. Always visible, thumb-height, 56px tall.
• Everything single column, nothing to pinch.
• Same 17px body text.
• Photos big enough to actually judge the work.

The two-button sticky bar is the highest-converting element on a trade site. It is worth more than any amount of styling above it.

DIRECTION D — RESTRAINT PASS

Too bright was fair. Going dark fixed the ground but left the loudest thing untouched: the accent was being used as full-bleed COLOUR FIELDS — a lime slab across the ticker, another across the whole closing CTA. On black that glows, and it reads young.

What changed:
• Accent is no longer a field. The ticker is now hairline rules with 5px dots; the closing CTA is dark with the accent on one button. Accent surface area is down roughly 90%.
• Acid lime is gone. Four mature options in its place — see the note to the right.
• Pure white → bone (#e8e4dd). Pure white on black glares; bone doesn't.
• Ground warmed from #0c0c0c to #0f0e0d. Slightly warm black reads as considered; neutral black reads as default.
• Photo placeholders warmed and dimmed to match.
• Hero dropped 132px → 118px. Still large, less shouting.
• The white safety panel became bone too, so it lands without flaring.

The bones are untouched: Archivo Black caps, square corners, heavy rules, the numbered index.

FOUR ADULT ACCENTS

All desaturated, all readable on bone and on black, none of them 'tech'.

• #a4432a OXBLOOD (default) — iron oxide. Rust is literally what happens to the material you work in, which is a better reason than most for a brand colour.
• #6d7f8c SLATE — cool, engineering, unshowy. The most corporate of the four.
• #8f9686 SAGE — muted green-grey. Quiet and land-adjacent; suits rural and estate work.
• #b8ab8e STONE — barely a colour. The most restrained option; the design carries itself on type and rules.

Try them from the tweak chip. Note the label colour flips automatically on the pale two so text stays readable.

If you want NO accent at all, pick Stone — at that point it is effectively tonal.

GALLERY + MOBILE

Same treatment: no accent slabs, bone type on warm black, accent reduced to filter pills, dots and one button.

The gallery is where this direction is strongest — twelve photos, 6px gutters, square corners, on near-black. It reads as one mass of work.

Auto-loading mechanism is untouched: drop files in /images/, sub-folders become filters. Only the skin changes.

Contact page follows the same rules; I'll build it with the rest.

FOUR DIRECTIONS — pick one, or pick bits of several

These are genuinely different aesthetics, not four shades of the same one. Judge them on how they FEEL for your business — the layouts are interchangeable, the personality isn't.

Each board shows a header, hero, work grid and the palette and fonts underneath.

The striped grey panels are photo placeholders.

You can also say "B but warmer" or "C's type on D's layout" — mixing is fine and often better than picking one whole.

A · YARD
Warm, plain-spoken, honest trade.

Bone paper, near-black ink, a burnt-orange accent. Chunky grotesk type. Reads like a good local firm that does solid work — approachable rather than expensive.

Best if most of your work is domestic and you want people to feel they can just ring you up.

B · BLUEPRINT
Technical, precise, engineered.

Paper white on a faint drafting grid, deep blue, monospace figures and dimension lines. Leans hard on the compliance story — the standards sit in the header band, not buried.

Best if you want commercial and security work, and to look like the firm that does it properly.

C · ESTATE
Quiet, refined, expensive.

Cream, ink, a muted olive. A modern serif set large and calm, generous space, centred composition. Lets one big photograph do the talking.

Best if you're chasing larger residential jobs — long driveways, bigger budgets, clients who compare on quality not price.

D · CONTRAST
Loud, confident, modern.

White, true black, and one electric accent. Enormous condensed caps, hard rules, tight image grid. Impossible to ignore and completely unlike any other gate company site.

Best if you want to look like the biggest, most modern outfit in the area. The riskiest of the four — strongest personality, least middle ground.

HOME — SIMPLIFIED  ← the new one

Nine sections cut to five. The photos do the selling; the copy gets out of the way.

• Full-bleed hero: one line, one button
• One sentence on how you work
• A big editorial grid of the work — mixed sizes, one running edge to edge
• Safety, stated once, with the numbers beside it
• One closing ask: "send us a photo of your driveway"

Gone: the four service cards, the four-step process, the testimonial row, the trust strip. All still available on their own pages.

This needs GOOD photography to work. With weak photos it will look emptier than the version on the right, not cleaner.

HOME — AS BUILT  ← the current one

This is what is live in the repo right now. Kept here for comparison.

More explanatory, more sections, more words. Safer if the photos aren't ready yet — the copy carries it.

GALLERY — the auto-loading bit
No hard-coded image list. A PHP script reads /images/ and builds this grid at page load.

Drop a JPEG in → it appears. Sub-folders become the filter buttons. Filenames become captions — and, for SEO, alt text.

The simplified home page pulls from the same folder, so it stays current on its own.

CONTACT
Form posts to a PHP handler on the same server and emails you — no third-party form service.

Honeypot, time-trap and per-IP rate limit built in. Works with JavaScript off.

HEAVILY SEO'd — what that actually means

You rank a page, not a site. Four pages can compete for about four phrases, so "heavy SEO" is mostly an ARCHITECTURE decision, not a markup one: roughly 28 pages instead of 4.

Read these three in order:
  1. Site architecture — the page tree and what each page targets
  2. Service page template — the anatomy that does the ranking
  3. Technical SEO spec — head tags, schema, images, build order

Two things I'd want you to read properly rather than skim: the doorway-page warning on board 1, and section 5 on board 3 — the part that isn't the website.

Nothing here is built yet. This is the plan to approve or cut down.

DECISIONS I NEED FROM YOU

• Which towns do you genuinely work in, in priority order?
• Which services earn the most, and which do you want more of? (Those get pages first.)
• Real price ranges — the single highest-value content on the site.
• Are you happy to commit to one guide a month? If not, we cut /guides/ from the plan rather than build a section that goes stale.

NOTE ON THE SIMPLIFIED HOME PAGE

A sparse, image-led home page has little text for Google to read. That is fine — but only because the six service pages do the ranking work.

If the SEO plan is cut and the home page is ALSO stripped back, the site has almost nothing to rank with. These two decisions are linked.
